segments.prompt:
2D hand-drawn cinematic single-character sequence, vertical 9:16, 15 seconds.

STYLE IDENTITY LOCK: preserve the exact identity, drawing language, proportions, materials and original colors of the approved Picture 1 mouse-ear mutant girl references. Keep her white short hair with eye-covering fringe and small upward curl, large translucent pale-violet mouse-ear mutation structures, small slender body, oversized pale short robe, dark collar, cuffs and hem blocks, diagonal strap and one side satchel. Preserve the verified identity, existing elements, spatial continuity and monochrome palette logic of Picture 2. Reference fidelity overrides generic style wording.

VISUAL EXPRESSION VARIABLE: use a restrained chest-up medium close-up to make the sequence of ear, eye and head reactions readable. Use compatible variable-weight linework, reference-consistent thin shading, soft diffuse light and quiet negative space only where compatible with the source images. Do not impose colors, materials or glow absent from the references.

CHARACTER (Picture 1): show exactly one physical instance of the established mouse-ear mutant girl. The half-body dynamic sheet and full-body identity sheet describe the same one person, never four people. Keep both mouse-ear mutation structures fully inside frame. Her torso remains still; only the ears, eyes and head make small movements.

ENVIRONMENT (Picture 2): preserve SCENE-01 as the same forest-lake location with its registered monochrome hierarchy. Picture 2 controls location identity and palette logic, not one mandatory crop. In the close background, use only soft supported tree, water, mist and open-space cues that are actually present. Do not invent a visible animal, person, machine, building, bridge, dock, sign, lamp or sound-producing object.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION: one fixed eye-level chest-up medium close-up in three-quarter view. Keep both mouse-ear structures, both eyes, the top of the diagonal strap and the upper robe readable. Leave quiet negative space on screen-left and screen-right for the two sound directions. The background remains softly subordinate but recognizably the same forest-lake scene. No push, pull, pan, tilt, cut or axis change.

ACTION: begin with the girl listening quietly, shoulders and torso still. A light natural breeze first moves the supported off-screen leaves on screen-left; her screen-left mouse-ear structure turns a small angle toward that sound while the other ear remains neutral. The leaf sound fades into a short quiet gap. A soft water-lap becomes clearer on screen-right; her screen-right ear then turns toward the water. Only after both ear reactions are readable do her eyes move from left to right. Her head follows by a few degrees and stops between the two directions. End with the torso unchanged, the ears held at two distinct attentive angles, and her cautious expression readable.

AUDIO DESIGN: quiet forest-lake air, one brief screen-left leaf rustle, a short near-silent gap, then soft screen-right water-lap and faint upper-robe settling. Use one very soft non-lyrical breath-like tone that begins after the second ear turns and fades when her head stops. Audio establishes direction and cautious attention; it is not a song, beat track or MV cue.

NEGATIVE: no second character, duplicate girl, clone, split screen, four-person character-sheet output, reflection person, shadow double or autonomous silhouette; no rabbit ears, ordinary replacement ears, tail, horns, wings, armor, weapon, new bag or changed robe; no cropped or missing mouse-ear structure, face drift or eye redesign; no visible animal or invented sound source; no walking, running, jumping, dancing, panic, exaggerated recoil or lip-sync; no camera movement, reframe, cut, axis flip or montage; no location replacement, glossy 3D render, hard synthetic digital edges, cyan-white energy humanoid, text, subtitle, logo or watermark.

segments.prompt:
2D hand-drawn cinematic single-character sequence, vertical 9:16, 15 seconds, continuing directly from the Work-selected real ending frame of Segment A.

STYLE IDENTITY LOCK: preserve the exact same Picture 1 mouse-ear mutant girl, including face, white short hair, translucent pale-violet mouse-ear mutation structures, small slender proportions, oversized pale short robe, dark edge blocks, diagonal strap, single side satchel, pale socks and oversized dark shoes. Preserve the same Picture 2 forest-lake identity, existing elements, monochrome hierarchy, lighting direction and original palette logic. Reference fidelity overrides generic style wording.

VISUAL EXPRESSION VARIABLE: begin from the inherited chest-up framing, then use one slow continuous pull-back to reveal a medium-wide full-body view before the step. Keep compatible variable-weight linework, reference-consistent thin shading, soft diffuse light and quiet negative space. Do not add colors or materials that conflict with either reference.

CHARACTER (Picture 1): show the same one physical girl from Segment A. Inherit the selected real A ending pose, ear angles, head direction, clothing state and satchel position. Her four reference views remain one identity. Do not begin the body movement until the pull-back has established both feet and supported ground.

ENVIRONMENT (Picture 2): remain in the same SCENE-01 space. The pull-back may reveal only existing visually supported ground, water, tree layers, mist and open space from Picture 2. Maintain the monochrome palette logic and the same screen directions. If Picture 2 cannot support this continuous reveal and one safe step direction, Work must not render this segment rather than inventing terrain.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION: inherit the exact eye-level three-quarter axis and close framing from Segment A. During the first four seconds, perform one slow continuous pull-back from chest-up medium close-up to a medium-wide full-body composition. Keep both ear structures visible throughout. Once both feet and the supported ground are readable, stop the camera completely. Preserve foreground ground, the character in the middle ground and forest-lake depth behind her. No cut, orbit, pan, tilt or axis flip.

ACTION: hold the inherited listening pose during the pull-back. When the camera settles, the screen-left leaf rustle has subsided and the screen-right water-lap remains soft and regular. Her two mouse-ear structures settle toward the quieter right-hand direction. Her eyes confirm that direction, then her head and shoulders align by a small amount. She shifts her weight without lifting both feet, slides the existing side satchel slightly closer with one forearm, and takes exactly one small step along the visually supported ground, parallel to the safe existing route rather than toward the water. The robe hem and satchel make one restrained follow-through and settle. End with both feet planted again, ears relaxed but attentive, and the same single character continuing calmly.

AUDIO DESIGN: continue the same forest-lake air and screen-right water-lap through the pull-back, then add one soft cloth press at the satchel, one small footfall and a brief robe-and-strap settling sound. The breath-like non-lyrical tone opens slightly at the weight shift and resolves when both feet plant. Audio supports the reveal, decision and landing; it is not a song cue, beat-synced edit or MV structure.

NEGATIVE: no second character, duplicate girl, clone, split screen, four-person character-sheet output, reflection person, shadow double or autonomous silhouette; no rabbit ears, ordinary replacement ears, tail, horns, wings, armor, weapon, new bag or changed robe; no visible animal, person or invented sound source; no body action before both feet and supported ground are established; no step toward or into water, extra steps, run, jump, dance, panic or lip-sync; no cut, orbit, pan, tilt, axis flip, reverse terrain, speed ramp or montage; no invented bridge, dock, stones, roots, building, sign, lamp or path; no location replacement, glossy 3D render, hard synthetic digital edges, cyan-white energy humanoid, text, subtitle, logo or watermark.
